changes.current_line: Support plans with tiered response times, up to 24/7 coverage.
changes.change: For buyers who run live on-sales, especially an operations or COO decider: "A name, not a queue." Someone who picks up. Name the solutions engineer and account lead who will be on the account, and put in writing what happens at minute four of an on-sale and who is on call for every major on-sale. Do not lead with tiers or response times. Only publish the on-call commitment once the team confirms it can staff it.
changes.why: The decider heard our tiers and response times as "a queue with a faster timer" and wanted a person, while the winning competitor promised named people and on-call coverage for every major on-sale.

changes.change: Add a written on-sale plan as a sales asset for ticketing and live-event buyers. It shows what we do on an on-sale morning: who is named on the account, who is on call, what the shared channel is, and what happens in the first minutes of a failure. Walk the operations decider through it directly, not only the technical champion.
changes.why: The decider "wanted to see, on paper, what we do on an on-sale morning", we had no such artifact, and the rep says it could have been built with the solutions engineer.

changes.current_line: Trusted by leading businesses; see our customer stories.
changes.change: For live-event and ticketing buyers: offer a conversation with a named customer who has run a real on-sale with us, instead of leading with logos or customer stories. Line: "Talk to someone who has been through an on-sale with us."
changes.why: The rep says "I had logos. I didn't have a person," and the customer asked "who," not for more proof of reliability.

changes.current_line: Built for developers: launch payments fast with our APIs, docs and sandbox.
changes.change: For a buyer who owns the consequences of a failure, pair the technical proof with the decider's framing: "I don't buy uptime, I buy what happens when it's down." Open the COO-facing conversation on who responds when payments fail during an on-sale, and treat the load test and sandbox story as support for the engineer, not the case for the decider.
changes.why: The load test went well with the CTO, but the COO decided in one meeting and said she does not buy uptime.
